sources.citation: Haspelmath, Martin, and Andrea D. Sims. 2010. Understanding Morphology. 2nd edition. London: Hodder Education. ISBN 9780340950012.
sources.license: Copyright; no open licence established
sources.summary: Introduces cross-language word structure rather than assuming one language’s categories. The publisher identifies both traditional concepts and current theory as its scope.
sources.use: Start with affix meaning, stem distribution and paradigm contrasts before choosing an MSA, slot or template. This is our application of that scope.
sources.limitation: Only publisher description and bibliographic metadata were inspected; this record is not a chapter-level digest.

sources.citation: Payne, Thomas E. 2006. Exploring Language Structure: A Student’s Guide. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. ISBN 9780521855426. Chapter 1, Introduction to morphology and syntax.
sources.license: Copyright Cambridge University Press; no open licence established
sources.quote: how meaningful units combine to shape words
sources.summary: Explains morphology as patterned word shapes that serve communicative purposes, and syntax as combinations of words. A comparable function may be expressed morphologically in one language and syntactically in another.
sources.use: Describe the intended contrast before equating a FLEx grammatical label with a universal category.
sources.limitation: The public chapter excerpt was inspected; no claims about the unread remainder of this or Payne’s 1997 book are made.

sources.citation: Bowern, Claire. 2015. Linguistic Fieldwork: A Practical Guide. 2nd edition. Palgrave Macmillan London. DOI 10.1057/9781137340801. ISBN 9781137340795.
sources.license: Copyright Palgrave Macmillan; subscription book, no open licence established
sources.summary: The overview and contents connect elicitation, morphology, lexical work, discourse, ethical research, data organization and archiving. Fieldwork includes returning usable materials to communities.
sources.use: The consultant’s job map covers the resulting materials and people as well as parser behavior.
sources.limitation: Overview and contents were inspected, not the subscription chapters. The personas and thirteen-job sequence are Motif design choices, not findings from this book.

sources.citation: Comrie, Bernard, Martin Haspelmath, and Balthasar Bickel. 2015. The Leipzig Glossing Rules: Conventions for interlinear morpheme-by-morpheme glosses. Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology and University of Leipzig. Revised February 2008; last change 31 May 2015.
sources.license: Public rules; no explicit open licence found on inspected page; excerpt only
sources.quote: Glosses are part of the analysis, not part of the data.
sources.summary: Conventions align morphemes and glosses and distinguish word boundaries, segmentation and category labels. Glossing encodes an analysis, which can differ between researchers.
sources.use: Keep observed forms, segmentation, gloss and translation distinct; do not treat a gloss as proof of one grammatical model.
sources.limitation: The September design permits reproduction, but this lane conservatively stores no full text without a verified open licence.

sources.citation: Black, H. Andrew. 2025. A Conceptual Introduction to Morphological Parsing for FieldWorks Language Explorer. SIL International, 3 July 2025. 108 PDF pages. FieldWorks 9 Help: Helps/WW-ConceptualIntro/ConceptualIntroFLEx.pdf.
sources.license: SIL-authored training prose; open redistribution licence not established
sources.summary: Explains inflectional templates, affix positions, category hierarchy, lexical inflection classes and grammatical features. Lexically selected allomorphs motivate inflection classes; category organization affects where those classes apply.
sources.use: Use sections 2.1.2.5–2.1.2.8 for MSA/category, class and feature decisions. Preserve attested contrasts when simplifying a grammar.
sources.limitation: Retrieved from canonical FieldWorks main; moving source, not a released parser pin. Store a content digest with any future task packet. No real-language examples are copied.

sources.citation: Black, H. Andrew. 2026. SIL Parser Workshop, session L02. Transcript distributed in FieldWorks Docs/ai-parser-help/workflow/sources/black-parser-workshop-2026-L02-fulltext.txt.
sources.license: SIL-authored workshop prose; open redistribution licence not established
sources.locator: How is it modeled in FLEx?, Inflection
sources.quote: The order of the slots constrains the order of the morphemes.
sources.summary: Walks from language evidence through lexicon and templates to parsing and iteration. Inflection uses templates; derivational descriptions state input and output categories.
sources.use: Teach one paradigm and check its positive and forbidden readings before extending the grammar.
sources.limitation: The session year is verified by its source index; no precise publication day established. A transcript’s UI descriptions require version-specific lookup.

sources.citation: Moe, Ronald, with revisions by others. 2016. Introduction to Lexicography for FieldWorks Language Explorer. SIL International. Original 11 November 2014; revised 11 October 2016.
sources.license: SIL-authored help prose; no open redistribution licence established
sources.summary: Connects collection, phonological and grammatical analysis, semantic description, entry management and publication. Lexicography requires multiple linguistic skills and supports community participation.
sources.use: Include lexicography and mother-tongue users in the consultant’s personas rather than treating all users as parser engineers.
sources.limitation: Public edition differs from the local 2025 revision mentioned in September research; this record cites only the inspected public 2016 edition.

sources.citation: SIL International. HCLoader.cs. FieldWorks, Src/LexText/ParserCore/HCLoader.cs, main branch, inspected 9 October 2026.
sources.license: LGPL-2.1-or-later, stated in file header
sources.summary: Loads FieldWorks grammar objects into HermitCrab, including category features, forms, inflection classes and templates. Storage objects and engine objects differ; source inspection explains projection but does not prove a particular imported grammar worked.
sources.use: Check loader reach and warnings before promising that a saved field changes parsing. Confirm the exact PanGloss importer separately.
sources.limitation: Moving main branch is contextual evidence only. Its strata support has changed relative to historical Motif notes; do not repeat their ceiling as a timeless fact.

sources.citation: SIL International. MasterLCModel.xml. SIL.LCModel NuGet package 11.0.0-beta0182, contentFiles/MasterLCModel.xml. Upstream: sillsdev/liblcm.
sources.license: LGPL-2.1-or-later; upstream liblcm LICENSE
sources.quote: a language optionally marks some feature-value combinations
sources.summary: The pinned model separates affix form, MSA, sense, slot and template. A slot can be optional; template prefix and suffix sequences are declared collections. Model prose describes intended modeling but is not evidence of loader coverage.
sources.use: Use MoStemMsa, MoInflAffMsa and MoDerivAffMsa as a terminology crosswalk, never as a low-level authoring recipe for an agent.
sources.limitation: The local package is authoritative for this record; the URL is a lookup entry, not that package’s immutable content. The package file digest is recorded in sources.json.

sources.citation: SIL International. Morpher.cs. SIL.Machine.Morphology.HermitCrab, sillsdev/machine master branch, inspected 9 October 2026.
sources.license: MIT; sillsdev/machine LICENSE
sources.summary: HermitCrab’s implementation includes analysis, lexical lookup and synthesis with surface matching. A proposed analysis must satisfy confirmation; a candidate enumeration alone does not demonstrate a valid reading.
sources.use: Distinguish PanGloss FST proposals from HermitCrab-confirmed analyses when constructing parser fact controls.
sources.limitation: Moving source does not prove behavior of the pinned PanGloss release. Future evidence must identify executable digest, mode, limits and completed search.

sources.license: Copyright; no open redistribution licence established

sources.summary: Distinguishes tasks, transcripts and actual outcomes. Recommends combining deterministic, model and human checks, calibrating model judgments, and beginning with a small suite of real failures.
sources.use: Judge frozen answers while control-side checks measure actual project outcomes. Keep capability and regression tasks visible.
sources.limitation: The source’s vocabulary is translated to Motif’s Episode and Trial distinctions. Its advice does not prescribe this recipe’s thresholds.

sources.citation: Anthropic. 2025-09-11. Writing effective tools for agents — with agents. Anthropic Engineering.
sources.license: Copyright; no open redistribution licence established
sources.quote: Returning meaningful context from tools back to agents
sources.summary: Uses tool prototypes, realistic tasks, transcript analysis and held-out cases to improve tools. Tool boundaries, descriptions and useful return content affect performance.
sources.use: Turn a surviving key attack into a concrete task control rather than relying on persuasive wording.
sources.limitation: Published practice motivates the loop; it does not validate Motif’s linguistic keys or authorize changing them during comparisons.
